description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each of these steps in order before proceeding (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

### Step 2: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry below as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `{project-root}` -- load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim (`_None._` means none):

- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md

### Step 3: Execute Append Steps

Execute each of these steps in order (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:

- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is self-contained and followed exactly
- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only load the current step file
- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping
- **State Tracking**: Persist progress via spec frontmatter and in-memory variables
- **Append-Only Building**: Build artifacts incrementally

### Step Processing Rules

1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Read the entire step file before acting
2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute sections in order
3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: Halt at checkpoints and wait for human
4. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file

### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

- **NEVER** load multiple step files simultaneously
- **ALWAYS** read entire step file before execution
- **NEVER** skip steps or optimize the sequence
- **ALWAYS** follow the exact instructions in the step file
- **ALWAYS** halt at checkpoints and wait for human input

762	### Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
763	
764	As a user,
765	I want to send a message to the assistant and get a response grounded in my own past Entries,
766	So that I feel genuinely understood rather than getting a generic reply.
767	
768	**Acceptance Criteria:**
769	
770	**Given** I type a message referencing something from weeks ago and send it
771	**When** the response streams in via SSE on `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`
772	**Then** it is grounded in semantic retrieval over my own Entries — not a stateless generic answer.
773	
774	**Given** the response is streaming
775	**When** it renders
776	**Then** exactly three visible states exist: streaming/processing (progressively revealed text behind a blinking cursor, chat-bubble component UX-DR4), error, complete.
777	
778	**Given** a Chat Message is sent
779	**When** it completes
780	**Then** it never automatically creates an Entry — RF10 (Story 6.4) is the sole, explicit exception.
781	**And** if Reduce Motion is enabled, the cursor-blink animation is skipped and the final text shows immediately instead (UX-DR24).
782	
783	### Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
784	
785	As a user,
786	I want to hold multiple named conversations and start a new one whenever I want a fresh start,
787	So that my chat history stays organized by topic or moment.
788	
789	**Acceptance Criteria:**
790	
791	**Given** I have existing Chat Sessions
792	**When** I open the side menu
793	**Then** they are listed and I can switch between them.
794	
795	**Given** I tap "Novo Chat" from the side menu
796	**When** a new session starts
797	**Then** it opens empty with the composer focused and the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no greeting copy invented beyond that.
798	
799	**Given** I am offline
800	**When** I attempt to start a new Chat Session
801	**Then** `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations.
802	**And** a returning (not new) session restores the last conversation's scroll position when I open it.
803	
804	### Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
805	
806	As a user,
807	I want a dropped response or an offline moment to never cost me my place in the conversation,
808	So that a flaky connection never feels like data loss.
809	
810	**Acceptance Criteria:**
811	
812	**Given** a response stream drops mid-generation
813	**When** the failure is detected
814	**Then** the partial message stays on screen with a failure indicator (timestamp slot replaced by red retry copy, bubble content never cleared).
815	
816	**Given** a dropped stream
817	**When** I tap retry
818	**Then** `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` regenerates the response without duplicating my original question.
819	
820	**Given** I am offline
821	**When** I view Home/Chat
822	**Then** the composer is disabled with the offline banner shown (UX-DR19), while existing conversation history stays visible and fully navigable/scrollable.

831	
832	**Given** one of my own Chat Messages (never an AI response)
833	**When** I tap the bookmark affordance

837	**When** the save executes

840	**Given** the bookmark button's four states (idle/saving/saved/error, UX-DR6)

# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.

## Stories

- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation

## Requirements & Constraints

- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.

## Technical Decisions

- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Home/Chat is still `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` — a non-functional placeholder. RF04's core promise (a conversation grounded in the user's own Entries via the real backend) doesn't exist yet.
16	
17	**Approach:** Build chat's first vertical slice (domain/data/presentation) to send a message and stream a RAG-grounded response over SSE, rendering exactly three per-message states (streaming, error, complete). Replace the placeholder screen with a minimal real one: header+drawer chrome reused, a message list, and a composer ("+" → existing `InsertionModal`, text field, send icon).

19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Exactly 3 visible message states: streaming (progressive text + blinking cursor, cursor skipped under `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`), error, complete. Bubble text is never cleared once any text streamed in, even on failure.
23	- `ChatRepository.sendMessage` returns `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>`; every other method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09).
24	- Call the backend only via `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>` (`chat-sessions-list`, `chat-sessions-create`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`) with `apikey` + `Bearer <user token>` headers, never the literal OpenAPI path.
25	- No connectivity → send resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`; never queued.
26	- Add streaming to the shared `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) instead of bypassing it — it stays the one façade every datasource calls through (AD-2/AD-5).
27	- Domain layer (`chat/domain`) imports neither `package:flutter` nor `chat/data` (RNF06).
28	- Chat's state is its own sealed class, never forced into `Resource<T>` (AD-12).
29	- On opening Home/Chat, silently ensure one Chat Session exists (reuse the most recent from `chat-sessions-list`, else `chat-sessions-create` with no title) — kept in memory only, no session-switcher UI (Story 6.2's job).
30	- Reuse `InsertionModal.show(...)` unchanged for the composer's "+".
31	
32	**Ask First:** none identified — session bootstrap is explicitly scoped to an in-memory value (see Design Notes) to avoid colliding with 6.2.
33	
34	**Never:** the retry-tap action / `chat-messages-retry` call, offline composer banner/lock, multi-session switcher, bookmark/save-to-journal button, insight card (all Stories 6.2–6.5); rendering the SSE `context` event's retrieval/citation data; any direct AI-provider call.

36	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
37	
38	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
39	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
40	| Happy path | Session exists, backend streams `message_created→token*→done` | Bubble fills progressively, ends `complete` | N/A |
41	| Mid-stream drop | Connection closes after some tokens, no `done`/`error` | Bubble keeps partial text, status `failed`, generic error indicator (not retry copy) | `Failure.networkTimeout` surfaced, no exception escapes |
42	| In-band `error` event | SSE emits `error` with a taxonomy code | Message marked `failed` | `Failure.fromCode(code, message)` |
43	| Send while offline | No connectivity | Send fails immediately, bubble marked `failed` | `Failure.networkOffline` |
44	| Bootstrap failure | `chat-sessions-list`/`create` fails on screen open | Screen shows a generic error state, not infinite spinner | Failure surfaced, no crash |

118	## Design Notes
119	
120	- SSE per-event field names aren't specified beyond the ordering `message_created→context→token*→done|error` (openapi.yaml:1257) — this spec assumes `token` carries a `delta` text field and `message_created` carries the persisted user-message id; anything that fails to parse as expected becomes `Failure.malformedResponse`, never a crash.
121	- A connection closing without a `done`/`error` event (mid-stream drop) is treated as `Failure.networkTimeout` — the taxonomy has no dedicated "dropped stream" code.
122	- Session bootstrap (list-or-create one session) is a minimal stand-in for Story 6.2's real session management: *which* session is the active one is kept in memory only (`ChatReady.sessionId`), never written to Hive as a dedicated "active session" record, so 6.2 can own that persistence shape without migrating this story's data. The `chat_sessions` Hive box itself does cache every session returned by `listSessions()`/`createSession()` (including the one this story's own bootstrap creates) — that's the ordinary offline read-cache the Code Map already calls for, not the active-session selection.

title: 'Story 6.1 — Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'done'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: 'f6eb83a3c07be75879b88469a6c962785f0eea24'
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Home/Chat is still `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` — a non-functional placeholder. RF04's core promise (a conversation grounded in the user's own Entries via the real backend) doesn't exist yet.

**Approach:** Build chat's first vertical slice (domain/data/presentation) to send a message and stream a RAG-grounded response over SSE, rendering exactly three per-message states (streaming, error, complete). Replace the placeholder screen with a minimal real one: header+drawer chrome reused, a message list, and a composer ("+" → existing `InsertionModal`, text field, send icon).

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Exactly 3 visible message states: streaming (progressive text + blinking cursor, cursor skipped under `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations`), error, complete. Bubble text is never cleared once any text streamed in, even on failure.
- `ChatRepository.sendMessage` returns `Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>>`; every other method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09).
- Call the backend only via `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>` (`chat-sessions-list`, `chat-sessions-create`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`) with `apikey` + `Bearer <user token>` headers, never the literal OpenAPI path.
- No connectivity → send resolves immediately to `Failure.networkOffline`; never queued.
- Add streaming to the shared `ApiClient` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`) instead of bypassing it — it stays the one façade every datasource calls through (AD-2/AD-5).
- Domain layer (`chat/domain`) imports neither `package:flutter` nor `chat/data` (RNF06).
- Chat's state is its own sealed class, never forced into `Resource<T>` (AD-12).
- On opening Home/Chat, silently ensure one Chat Session exists (reuse the most recent from `chat-sessions-list`, else `chat-sessions-create` with no title) — kept in memory only, no session-switcher UI (Story 6.2's job).
- Reuse `InsertionModal.show(...)` unchanged for the composer's "+".

**Ask First:** none identified — session bootstrap is explicitly scoped to an in-memory value (see Design Notes) to avoid colliding with 6.2.

**Never:** the retry-tap action / `chat-messages-retry` call, offline composer banner/lock, multi-session switcher, bookmark/save-to-journal button, insight card (all Stories 6.2–6.5); rendering the SSE `context` event's retrieval/citation data; any direct AI-provider call.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path | Session exists, backend streams `message_created→token*→done` | Bubble fills progressively, ends `complete` | N/A |
| Mid-stream drop | Connection closes after some tokens, no `done`/`error` | Bubble keeps partial text, status `failed`, generic error indicator (not retry copy) | `Failure.networkTimeout` surfaced, no exception escapes |
| In-band `error` event | SSE emits `error` with a taxonomy code | Message marked `failed` | `Failure.fromCode(code, message)` |
| Send while offline | No connectivity | Send fails immediately, bubble marked `failed` | `Failure.networkOffline` |
| Bootstrap failure | `chat-sessions-list`/`create` fails on screen open | Screen shows a generic error state, not infinite spinner | Failure surfaced, no crash |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1156-1306` -- `chat.messages.list/send/retry`, `chat.sessions.list/create`: x-cerne-function names, request/response schemas, SSE order `message_created→context→token*→done|error` (no per-event field schema given).
- `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` -- closed 13-code set; `NETWORK_OFFLINE` never an actual HTTP response.
- `docs/input/requirements.md:30-35` -- RF04 AC (3 states; dropped stream keeps partial text); `:170-179` -- endpoint-to-RF04 table.
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:14-83` -- sealed `Failure`, `retryable`, `Failure.fromCode`.
- `lib/core/resource.dart:1-33` -- doc comment explicitly excludes RF04's chat stream from `Resource<T>`.
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:27-148` -- façade to extend with a streaming method; mirror `_send`/`_mapDioException` (88-127) for error mapping.
- `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:84-92` -- feature-registration call order to extend with `registerChatFeature()`.
- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart:20-84`, `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`, `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart`, `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- DI/Hive-box convention and Either-construction/DTO-parse pattern to mirror for chat's non-streaming calls.
- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart:27,39,51,60,66,90,201-210` -- `colorAccent`, `colorSurfaceElevated`, `colorError`, `colorInfoOffline`, `colorChatBubbleUser`, `colorErrorBg`, radii.
- `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart:56-78` -- Reduce Motion pattern to mirror for the streaming cursor.
- `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:105-108` -- swap `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` for the real `ChatScreen`.
- `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart:78-150` -- `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` (header/drawer/composer-trigger chrome to reuse, then delete the class).
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:40`, `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart:19` -- stale doc-comment mentions of `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` to fix.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:257-268` -- existing fake-cubit DI-override pattern (`MeusRegistrosCubit`) to mirror for `ChatCubit`; same file has 13 `find.byType(HomeChatPlaceholderScreen)` assertions (incl. `test/main_test.dart`, `test/core/navigation/placeholder_screens_test.dart:143-192`) needing the swap.
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md:63-70` -- Tela 1 visual states (default/streaming/falha/offline).

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- add `Stream<Either<Failure,String>> postStream(...)` via `ResponseType.stream`, reusing `_mapDioException` -- keeps ApiClient the one façade; SSE line-splitting stays feature-local.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/{chat_session,chat_message,chat_stream_event}.dart` -- `ChatSession`, `ChatMessage` (role/status enums), sealed `ChatStreamEvent` (`messageCreated`/`token`/`done`) -- no flutter import (RNF06).
- [x] `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` -- abstract `ChatRepository`: `listSessions()`, `createSession()`, `listMessages(sessionId)` (`Future<Either<Failure,T>>`), `sendMessage(sessionId, content)` (`Stream<Either<Failure,ChatStreamEvent>>`).
- [x] `lib/features/chat/data/models/{chat_session_dto,chat_message_dto}.dart` -- `json_serializable` DTOs + `toEntity()`, mirroring `entry_dto.dart`.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart` -- non-streaming calls via `ApiClient` JSON methods; `sendMessage` via `postStream`, parsing `event:`/`data:` blocks into `ChatStreamEvent`s, mapping an in-band `error` event through `Failure.fromCode` and an unterminated close to `Failure.networkTimeout`; `context` event received and discarded.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart` -- implement `ChatRepository`; Hive box cache for `listSessions`/`listMessages` (local fallback), same convention as `entries_injection.dart`.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart` + `injection_container.dart:92` -- `registerChatFeature()` opening the chat Hive box and registering datasource/repository/cubit.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/{chat_state,chat_cubit}.dart` -- sealed `ChatState` (bootstrap loading/ready/error + append-only message list with per-message streaming/complete/failed); `ChatCubit.init()` (bootstrap session+history) and `.sendMessage(content)` (optimistic user bubble, subscribe to repo stream, append tokens, finalize/fail, never clear text on failure).
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart` -- user (`colorChatBubbleUser`, squared bottom-right) vs AI (`colorSurfaceElevated`, squared bottom-left) bubble; blinking cursor skipped under Reduce Motion; failure indicator (`colorError`/`colorErrorBg`) replaces timestamp slot on `failed`.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- real screen: same header/drawer chrome as the former placeholder; composer row ("+" → `InsertionModal.show` unchanged, text field placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon → `cubit.sendMessage`).
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart:107` -- `ChatScreen(cubit: sl<ChatCubit>())` replacing `const HomeChatPlaceholderScreen()`.
- [x] `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart` -- delete the now-unused `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen`.
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:40`, `entry_record_card.dart:19` -- fix the stale comment mentions.
- [x] `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/main_test.dart`, `test/core/navigation/placeholder_screens_test.dart` -- swap `find.byType(HomeChatPlaceholderScreen)` → `ChatScreen`; add a fake-`ChatRepository`-backed `ChatCubit` DI override mirroring `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s (lines 257-268); drop the placeholder's own test group.
- [x] `test/features/chat/**` -- unit tests for `ChatRepositoryImpl` (SSE parsing incl. drop/offline/error-event cases) and `ChatCubit` (3-state transitions, append-only-on-error) covering the I/O matrix.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given an existing session with prior messages, when Home/Chat opens, then history loads (cache-first where offline-readable) and the composer is enabled.
- Given no session exists yet, when Home/Chat opens, then exactly one session is silently created and reused for subsequent sends.
- Given a message referencing a weeks-old Entry, when the response streams, then it is grounded in semantic retrieval end-to-end against the real backend.
- Given a response is streaming, when it renders, then only streaming/error/complete are visible, with Reduce Motion skipping the cursor blink.
- Given a stream drops or returns an in-band error, when detected, then the partial bubble text is never cleared and no exception escapes the cubit.

### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [x] [Review][Patch] New `ApiClient.postStream`/`_mapStreamDioException` `AUTH_EXPIRED` → `SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` branch has zero test coverage — the sibling non-stream path (`_mapDioException`) is fully covered by the existing Story 1.5 test group, but none of the 6 new `postStream` tests construct an `AUTH_EXPIRED` in-band stream error, so a regression in this duplicated branch (e.g. a mid-chat token expiry) would silently fail to surface the re-auth overlay with no test catching it. [lib/core/network/api_client.dart:171]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatCubit.close()` cancels `_sendSubscription` without completing the in-flight `sendMessage()`'s `Completer` — `StreamSubscription.cancel()` never fires `onDone`/`onError`, so closing the cubit mid-send leaves that `Future` permanently unresolved (a leak, currently unobserved since no caller awaits it — see the related finding below). [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:279-282]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatRemoteDataSource.sendMessage()` normalizes `\r\n` → `\n` on each raw chunk *before* appending to `buffer` (`buffer += chunk.replaceAll('\r\n', '\n')`), so a `\r\n` line ending split exactly across two stream chunks (chunk ends `\r`, next starts `\n`) is never normalized — the literal `\r\n` survives inside `buffer`, risking a corrupted event-name/data-line parse (a spurious `malformedResponse`/failed bubble) for that message. Fix: concatenate first, then normalize the whole buffer. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:119]
- [x] [Review][Patch] "Most recent session" selection (`ChatCubit._bootstrap()`) and the offline-cache session ordering (`ChatRepositoryImpl._cachedSessions()`) both sort via raw `String.compareTo` on the `updatedAt` ISO-8601 field, diverging from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s own convention of `DateTime.parse(...).compareTo(...)` for the same kind of timestamp — any drift in fractional-second precision or offset notation between records would silently reorder which session counts as "most recent," with no error surfaced. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:76, lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:143]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatRemoteDataSource.listSessions()`/`listMessages()` parse the live response in one all-or-nothing `try`/`catch` around `data.map(...).toList()` — a single malformed item discards every other valid session/message in that response (`Left(malformedResponse)` for the whole call), while the offline-cache fallback (`ChatRepositoryImpl._cachedSessions`/`_cachedMessages`) explicitly decodes item-by-item and skips just the bad one. The live path is strictly worse-handled than the same data once cached — apply the same per-item isolation to the live parse step. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:24-43,60-81]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `RetryInterceptor`'s new `neverRetriedFunctions` exclusion tests (`retry_interceptor_test.dart`) build `DioException`s with bare paths like `/chat-messages-send`, but the real call always goes through `pathParams: [sessionId]`, producing `/chat-messages-send/{sessionId}`. The exclusion happens to still work today because `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf` only reads the first path segment, but nothing proves the exclusion against that actual trailing-segment shape. [test/core/network/retry_interceptor_test.dart:169]
- [x] [Review][Patch] This story's own Design Notes say chat-session bootstrap is "kept in memory only, never persisted to a Hive entry," but `ChatRepositoryImpl.createSession()`/`listSessions()` do write every session (including the one bootstrap just created) to the `chat_sessions` Hive box — the Code Map's own separate instruction ("Hive box cache for `listSessions`/`listMessages`") confirms this caching is intentional and correct, so the code isn't wrong; the Design Notes wording is. Reword to scope "in memory only" to the active-session *selection*, not the cache. [Design Notes, below]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_ChatComposer`'s doc comment claims the composer is "Disabled as a whole while the bootstrap hasn't resolved yet or while an AI bubble is still streaming," but the "+" `IconButton` (`InsertionModal.show`) is never gated by `canSend` — only the text field and send button are. Functionally this mirrors the deleted placeholder's own always-tappable "+", which is plausibly correct; the comment is what's wrong. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:208-211]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `entry_record_card.dart`'s Code-Map-mandated stale-comment fix replaces one stale `HomeChatPlaceholderScreen` reference with a new inaccurate one — it claims `Icons.chat_bubble_outline` is now used by `ChatScreen`'s `_ChatBootstrapErrorView`, but that view actually renders `Icons.error_outline`; no icon in the new `ChatScreen` uses `chat_bubble_outline`. [lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entry_record_card.dart:18-20]

**Defer:**
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_ChatBootstrapErrorView` renders every bootstrap-failure cause (offline, timeout, server error) identically via `colorError`, even though the spec's own Code Map lists `colorInfoOffline` as a relevant token for this story and it's never referenced anywhere in the diff — no acceptance criterion requires differentiated styling per cause. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:173-204] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatScreen`'s `BlocConsumer` listener calls `_scrollToBottomSoon()` on every `ChatReady` emission, which fires once per streamed token — a long AI response registers a fresh `addPostFrameCallback` on nearly every frame. Harmless today (cheap, idempotent `jumpTo`), but unthrottled. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:64] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The composer's client-side 8000-char cap (`TextField(maxLength: 8000, ...)`) assumes the backend counts `content` length the same way Flutter's `maxLength` does; nothing in this diff confirms the backend's own counting unit, and this can't be verified from the client repo alone. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:253] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] No test drives an `authExpired` bootstrap failure through `ChatCubit`/`ChatScreen` — the underlying re-auth-overlay trigger is already covered generically by Story 1.5's `_mapDioException` test group (which `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` all go through), so this is a thin-spot regression test, not a live gap. [test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The streaming AI bubble (`ChatBubble`) renders growing text via plain `Text.rich` with no `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` — a screen-reader user gets no incremental announcement while tokens stream in. Same unaddressed accessibility pattern already deferred for other widgets elsewhere in this codebase; no accessibility requirement is scoped for this story. [lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The two new `chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` Hive boxes accumulate every session/message ever fetched with no eviction/TTL — the same unbounded-growth pattern already deferred for the `entries` Hive box (spec-4-1). [lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

Harmless today (nothing throws after that await point), but a future story (e.g. 6.5's insight-trigger counting) adding logic there would have its errors/results silently dropped unless the call site starts awaiting. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:55] — deferred, pre-existing

**Reject (noise, dropped):** Unguarded `Hive.openBox<Map>()` calls in `chat_injection.dart` and the lack of a retry affordance on `ChatBootstrapError` were both independently raised by two review layers each, but both are already self-disclosed in `deferred-work.md` by this story's own commit — the Hive-open gap as a pre-existing cross-cutting pattern shared with `entries_injection.dart`, and the no-retry gap as satisfying the written I/O matrix ("a generic error state, not infinite spinner") rather than a regression. Handled elsewhere; not re-added here.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- SSE per-event field names aren't specified beyond the ordering `message_created→context→token*→done|error` (openapi.yaml:1257) — this spec assumes `token` carries a `delta` text field and `message_created` carries the persisted user-message id; anything that fails to parse as expected becomes `Failure.malformedResponse`, never a crash.
- A connection closing without a `done`/`error` event (mid-stream drop) is treated as `Failure.networkTimeout` — the taxonomy has no dedicated "dropped stream" code.
- Session bootstrap (list-or-create one session) is a minimal stand-in for Story 6.2's real session management: *which* session is the active one is kept in memory only (`ChatReady.sessionId`), never written to Hive as a dedicated "active session" record, so 6.2 can own that persistence shape without migrating this story's data. The `chat_sessions` Hive box itself does cache every session returned by `listSessions()`/`createSession()` (including the one this story's own bootstrap creates) — that's the ordinary offline read-cache the Code Map already calls for, not the active-session selection.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass, including new chat tests and updated navigation tests
- `fvm flutter pub run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs` -- expected: regenerates chat DTOs' `.g.dart` with no conflicts

**Streaming transport (SSE + network layer)**

  [`api_client.dart:108`](../../lib/core/network/api_client.dart#L108)

  [`api_client.dart:131`](../../lib/core/network/api_client.dart#L131)

- Review fix: excludes the two non-idempotent chat POSTs from transparent retry, which could otherwise silently resend a message.
  [`retry_interceptor.dart:36`](../../lib/core/network/retry_interceptor.dart#L36)

**Chat state machine (bootstrap + send guard)**

- Concurrency-safe session bootstrap — a second concurrent call reuses the same in-flight future, never creates two sessions.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:51`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L51)

- Review fix: the send-in-flight guard is its own field now, not derived from scanning loaded messages' persisted status.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:130`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L130)

- Clears the guard and the UI-facing signal together, the one place both flip back after a send ends.
  [`chat_cubit.dart:200`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart#L200)

- The composer's one enable/disable signal — a dedicated field, not a scan over message statuses.
  [`chat_state.dart:61`](../../lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart#L61)

**Offline cache resilience**

- Review fix: one corrupted cache entry is skipped per-item now, instead of discarding the whole cached list.
  [`chat_repository_impl.dart:132`](../../lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart#L132)

- Review fix: a local cache-write failure after a successful remote create no longer masks that success as an error.
  [`chat_repository_impl.dart:64`](../../lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart#L64)

**Screen & UI wiring**

  [`app_router.dart:109`](../../lib/core/navigation/app_router.dart#L109)

**Peripherals (DI, tokens, tests)**

input.prompt:
I'm planning Story 6.2 "Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation" for a Flutter app (Cerne, Clean Architecture, flutter_bloc). Story 6.1 (send message + RAG streaming response) just shipped the chat feature's first vertical slice. I need a distilled investigation report (file paths + line numbers + short notes only, no long quotes) covering the following, so I can write an implementation spec without re-deriving it later:

**Acceptance criteria I'm implementing (verbatim from epics.md):**
- Given I have existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they are listed and I can switch between them.
- Given I tap "Novo Chat" from the side menu, when a new session starts, then it opens empty with the composer focused and placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- Given I am offline, when I attempt to start a new Chat Session, then POST /chat/sessions is blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations.
- A returning (not new) session restores the last conversation's scroll position when opened.

**1. Current chat feature state (post-6.1), read these fully:**
- lib/features/chat/domain/entities/*.dart (ChatSession, ChatMessage, ChatStreamEvent shapes)
- lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart (existing abstract methods: listSessions, createSession, listMessages, sendMessage — exact signatures)
- lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart (Hive caching convention, how listSessions/createSession work, line numbers)
- lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart (how listSessions/createSession call the backend — x-cerne-function names used)
- lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart (DI registration, Hive box names)
- lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart and chat_cubit.dart (current sealed state shape, bootstrap logic — the "silently ensure one session exists, reuse most recent" logic and its exact line numbers, since 6.2 needs to replace/extend this with real session switching)
- lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart (header/drawer wiring, composer, scroll controller usage if any)

**2. Side menu / drawer:**
- lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart — full structure, how menu items are currently built, where a session list / "Novo Chat" entry would plausibly go, any existing scrollable list pattern inside it.

**3. Offline detection pattern already used in the codebase** (for reuse, not reinvention) — search for how the existing offline composer lock or offline banner (mentioned in epic context) is implemented, e.g. grep for "networkOffline", "offline", "NetworkInfo", "connectivity" across lib/features/chat and lib/core. Report exact file:line of whatever decides "are we offline" today.

**4. Backend contract for chat sessions** — read docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml around the chat.sessions paths (list/create) and report: exact x-cerne-function names, request/response schemas, whether there's any session-rename/delete endpoint, and whether list is paginated/cursor-based. Also check docs/input/backend/README.md for the path-to-function mapping table entries for chat sessions.

**5. Requirements doc** — docs/input/requirements.md: find the FR-24 section (multi-session chat history) and the endpoint-to-requirement mapping table rows for chat sessions endpoints, report line numbers and verbatim short excerpts only for FR-24's own text.

**6. Prototype extract** — docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md: search for side menu / "Novo Chat" / session list / drawer visual states, report line numbers and token names (colors/spacing) if specified; note if it's silent (in which case I'll need to decide per AGENTS.md policy).

**7. Existing test conventions for chat** — list test/features/chat/** files that exist, and note the DI-override/fake-repository pattern used in test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart around lines 257-268 (mentioned in spec-6-1 as the pattern to mirror) — just confirm it's still there and report the exact current line range.

**8. Scroll-position precedent** — grep the codebase for any existing ScrollController persistence pattern (e.g. in entries list) that could be mirrored for "restore last scroll position."

Report everything as a compact structured list grouped by section number above, with file:line citations. Do not include code review opinions — just facts I need to write a spec. Keep total report under 700 lines of output.

  - `listMessages(sessionId)` (66-92) calls `_apiClient.get('chat-messages-list', pathParams: [sessionId])`.
  - `sendMessage(sessionId, content)` (114-163) calls `_apiClient.postStream('chat-messages-send', pathParams: [sessionId], data: {'content': content})`; SSE parsing in `_parseEvent` (177-248).
  - x-cerne-function names used by this client today: `chat-sessions-list`, `chat-sessions-create`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`. `chat-messages-retry` and `chat-insight-create` (contract-defined, §4) are **not yet called anywhere in this file** — Story 6.3/6.5's job.
  
  **DI** (`lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart`)
  - Hive box name constants: `chatSessionsBoxName = 'chat_sessions'` (14), `chatMessagesBoxName = 'chat_messages'` (15).
  - `registerChatFeature()` (22-54): opens both boxes (23-24), registers them as named `Box<Map>` singletons (29-30), registers `ChatRemoteDataSource`/`ChatRepository` as lazy singletons (32-42), registers `ChatCubit` as a lazy singleton with `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` (50-53) — doc (44-49) explains this is deliberate so a bootstrapped session survives navigating away and back within the same app run. **This lazySingleton-cubit shape is the thing 6.2 most needs to reconcile**: switching sessions / starting new ones must mutate this one long-lived cubit's state rather than re-resolving a fresh cubit per screen visit.
  
  **Cubit state** (`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart`)
  - Sealed `ChatState` (9-11): `ChatBootstrapLoading` (16-18), `ChatBootstrapError(failure)` (23-35), `ChatReady(sessionId, messages, isSending=false)` (40-69) — **no `List<ChatSession>` anywhere in this state**, i.e. there is currently no state slice for "the list of sessions to show in the drawer." 6.2 will need to add one (either to `ChatReady` or a new field/event).
  - `ChatUiMessage` (78-115): presentation-layer message shape with locally-generated `id`.
  
  **Cubit logic** (`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`)
  - `init()` (57-62): no-op once `state is ChatReady`; otherwise kicks off `_bootstrap()`, deduped via `_initFuture` (49, 61) so concurrent mounts don't double-bootstrap.
  - `_bootstrap()` (64-114) — **the exact "silently ensure one session exists, reuse most recent" logic 6.2 must replace/extend**:
    - 65: emits `ChatBootstrapLoading`.
    - 67: calls `_repository.listSessions()`.
    - 71-87: if `sessions.isEmpty` → `_repository.createSession()` (74); else re-sorts by `updatedAt` desc defensively (81-86) and picks `mostRecent.first` (86) — this is the "reuse the most recent" rule.
    - 92-113: on session resolved, calls `listMessages(session.id)` and emits `ChatReady(sessionId, messages)`.
    - This entire method has **no notion of "the user picked session X from the drawer"** — it always auto-picks. 6.2 needs a new public method (e.g. `switchSession(String sessionId)` / `startNewSession()`) that bypasses this auto-pick and explicitly loads/creates a given session, while leaving `init()`'s existing auto-bootstrap behavior intact for first load.
  - `sendMessage()` (139-206): guarded by `current is! ChatReady`, `_isSending` (148-150) — no offline check of its own; offline surfaces only as a stream `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` from the repository/ApiClient layer (see §3), not a pre-emptive UI lock.
  - `close()` (291-299) cancels `_sendSubscription` and completes any pending `_sendCompleter`.
  
  **Chat screen** (`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`)
  - `ChatScreen` takes `cubit` as a constructor param, not resolved internally (22-23) — "so a test can pass a fake-repository-backed instance directly" (18-21).
  - `_scrollController = ScrollController()` (33), created fresh every mount, disposed in `dispose()` (44-48) — **no scroll-offset persistence of any kind**.
  - `_scrollToBottomSoon()` (59-79): only auto-scrolls to bottom if already near-bottom or not yet attached; this is "stick to bottom while streaming," unrelated to "restore last scroll position for a returning session" (6.2's own AC).
  - `drawer: const AppDrawer()` (87), `drawerScrimColor: DesignTokens.colorScrimHeavy` (88-91).
  - Composer `_ChatComposer` (214-316): `enabled: canSend` where `canSend = state is ChatReady && !state.isSending` (224) — composer disable today is purely about "a send is in flight," not offline; explicit comment (211-213) "never a dedicated offline banner/lock, that's Story 6.3's job."
  - `_ChatBootstrapErrorView` (173-204): generic error view, "no retry action exists yet (Boundaries: the retry-tap action belongs to Story 6.2–6.5)" (170-172) — confirms 6.2 is in scope for some bootstrap-error handling improvement too, per that comment's own numbering.
  
  ## 2. Side menu / drawer (`lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`)
  
  - Doc comment (8-16) is explicit: **currently there is no CONVERSAS/past-session list — RF04/RF07 aren't built into the drawer yet**; only a static "Novo Chat" action that just closes the drawer (14-16, 65-71).
  - `AppDrawer` is a `StatefulWidget` (17-22) with one guard field `_actionTaken` (30) to prevent double-pop races (25-29).
  - `build()` (33-113): `Drawer(width: DesignTokens.drawerWidth, ...)` (34-37), no `SafeArea` (comment 39-43 explains why — fixed-frame design, `drawerContentPadding` already accounts for status bar).
  - Structure: header `Row` with `Avatar` + static "Usuário" text (49-63) → `_DrawerPrimaryAction` "Novo Chat" (65-71, currently just `_closeDrawer`) → a bordered second section (`Container` with `border: top`, 78-108) containing three `_DrawerNavItem`s: Meus Registros (88-93), Planos de Ação (94-99), Configurações (100-105).
  - **No existing scrollable list pattern inside this drawer** — everything is a fixed `Column`, not a `ListView`/`Expanded`. A session list would need to go between the "Novo Chat" primary action (65-71) and the bordered nav-items section (78-108), inside its own bordered block per the prototype's "CONVERSAS" section (see §6), and would need to become scrollable (wrap in `Expanded`+`ListView` or similar) since the Column currently has no bounded/scrollable child.
  - `_closeDrawer`/`_navigate` (115-130) are the only navigation primitives; a "switch session" tap handler would plausibly follow the `_navigate`-style guard-then-pop pattern but calling into `ChatCubit` instead of `context.go(...)`.
  - `_DrawerPrimaryAction` (133-178) and `_DrawerNavItem` (180-216) are the two existing list-item widget shapes available to mirror for a per-session row.
  
  ## 3. Offline detection pattern (reuse, not reinvention)
  
  - **There is no `NetworkInfo`/`Connectivity` class anywhere in `lib/`** — confirmed by grep across `lib/` for `networkOffline|NetworkOffline|isOffline|connectivity|NetworkInfo|Connectivity`. The app has no proactive "are we online" check; offline is only ever *discovered* retroactively, when a real HTTP call fails.
  - The actual offline decision point: `lib/core/network/dio_error_code.dart:14-33`, function `dioErrorCodeOf(DioException e)`. Logic: checks `e.response?.data['code']` first (15-18); then maps `connectionTimeout/sendTimeout/receiveTimeout` → `'NETWORK_TIMEOUT'` (20-23); `cancel` → `null` (24-25); **else if `e.response == null` → `'NETWORK_OFFLINE'`** (29-31) — i.e. "offline" is inferred purely from "the HTTP call never got an HTTP response at all," not from a device connectivity API.
  - `ApiClient._send()` (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart:184+`, not fully read but referenced) is what turns a thrown `DioException` into `Failure.networkOffline(...)` via this code.
  - `Failure.networkOffline` factory: `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:19-20`; code string mapping `'NETWORK_OFFLINE' => Failure.networkOffline(...)`: `lib/core/failure/failure.dart:71`.
  - Existing reuse convention for "offline → fallback to cache" (what `ChatRepositoryImpl.listSessions/listMessages` already do): `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:75-81,111-115,151` — same `if (failure is NetworkOffline || failure is NetworkTimeout)` branch shape chat already mirrors.
  - **There is no pre-flight "is the device online" check used to proactively disable the composer or block `createSession()` before firing the request.** FR-25/FR-27's "offline composer lock" (epics.md lines 66, 804-822 — Story 6.3) is **not implemented yet anywhere in the current code** — `ChatScreen`'s composer-disable logic (`chat_screen.dart:224`) is solely `state is ChatReady && !state.isSending`, with an explicit comment (211-213) that offline lock is Story 6.3's job. **This means Story 6.2's AC "blocked, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations" is referencing a UI mechanism that doesn't exist in the codebase yet** — 6.2 can only make `createSession()` behaviorally blocked offline (already true today, repository-side, no cache fallback) but cannot visually/consistently reuse a lock UI that Story 6.3 hasn't built. Worth flagging explicitly in the spec as a forward dependency / sequencing note.
  
  ## 4. Backend contract — `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`
  
  - `POST /chat/sessions` (1000-1070): `operationId: chat.sessions.create` (1002), `x-cerne-function: chat-sessions-create` (1006). Request body: optional `title` (minLength 1) (1013-1016) — **optional, so the client choosing to send none, as it does today, is contract-valid.** Response `data`: `id, title, personaSnapshot (enum analitico/empatico/socratico), userMessageCount, lastUserMessageAt (nullable date-time), createdAt, updatedAt` (1026-1059), all required.
  - `GET /chat/sessions` (1071-1155): `operationId: chat.sessions.list` (1072), `x-cerne-function: chat-sessions-list` (1076). **Is cursor-paginated**: query params `cursor` (optional string, 1078-1082) and `limit` (optional int, 1-50, default 20, 1083-1090). Response `meta.nextCursor` (nullable string, required, 1139-1146) and `meta.total` (int, 1142-1144, not marked required). **The current `ChatRemoteDataSource.listSessions()` passes neither `cursor` nor `limit`** — only ever fetches page 1 of ≤20 sessions; 6.2's drawer session list will only show the first page unless pagination is added.
  - No rename or delete endpoint exists for sessions anywhere in the spec — full endpoint inventory for chat found: `chat.sessions.create` (1002), `chat.sessions.list` (1072), `chat.messages.list` (1158), `chat.messages.send` (1231), `chat.messages.retry` (1270, path `/chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry`), `chat.insight.create` (not fully read, path `/chat/sessions/{id}/insight`, ~1307-1313). **No `PATCH`/`DELETE` on `/chat/sessions` or `/chat/sessions/{id}`.**
  - `docs/input/backend/README.md` path→function table rows for chat (34-38): `POST /chat/sessions → chat-sessions-create`; `GET /chat/sessions → chat-sessions-list`; `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/messages → chat-messages-list`; `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages → chat-messages-send`; `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry → chat-messages-retry`; `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight → chat-insight-create`. README line 20 explains the general URL-building rule (no router — functions are called at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>`, path params appended as trailing segments).
  
  ## 5. Requirements doc (`docs/input/requirements.md`)
  
  - **"FR-24" does not exist in `requirements.md`** — that numbering (`FR-24: Multi-session chat history`) only exists in `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md:63` and `epics.md:215`. `requirements.md` uses `RF01`–`RF10` numbering instead; the closest/only matching section is **RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)**, `requirements.md:30-35`:
    - Line 30: `### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)`
    - Line 31: "Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10."
    - Lines 33-35 (Acceptance criteria): "Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response." / "If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear)." — **RF04's own AC text says nothing about multi-session/new-conversation**; that's entirely epics.md's own FR-24/FR-25 breakdown, not sourced from an RF04 AC line.
  - Endpoint→requirement mapping table rows for chat sessions (`requirements.md:173-178`):
    - 173: `POST /chat/sessions — blocked offline | RF04 | —`
    - 174: `GET /chat/sessions — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | —`
    - 175: `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages — works offline (cache) | RF04 | —`
    - 176: `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI + Claude Sonnet 5`
    - 177: `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry ... | RF04 | Voyage AI + Claude Sonnet 5`
    - 178: `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5`
  - RF07 (`requirements.md:54`) is "Multi-source history (timeline)" — Meus Registros's own cross-source feed, unrelated to chat session switching despite being co-listed on line 174 (co-listed only because `GET /chat/sessions` happens to also feed RF07's timeline per that table's own semantics, not because RF07 covers the drawer UI).
  - **Actual FR-24 source text** (for the spec's citation, since it isn't in requirements.md): `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md:63`: "FR-24: Multi-session chat history — multiple named Chat Sessions, listed and switchable from the side menu." Adjacent: line 64 "FR-25: New-conversation action — start a new Chat Session from the side menu; `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline." Line 65 "FR-26: Dropped-stream resilience..." Line 66 "FR-27: Offline composer lock — composer disabled while offline; existing conversation history stays visible and navigable" (confirms §3's finding — FR-27/Story 6.3 is a separate, not-yet-built story). Story 6.2's own AC block: `epics.md:783-802`.
  
  ## 6. Prototype extract (`docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`)
  
  - Line 25: nav map — `side menu (☰ icon) ──> Meus Registros | Planos de Ação | Configurações | new conversation`.
  - **Line 70 is the only mention of the session list**: `| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |` — confirms: section header literal "CONVERSAS", each row shows **title + timestamp** (no other metadata — no preview text, no unread indicator, no persona icon mentioned).
  - No color/spacing token is specified anywhere for this CONVERSAS section or its row items (no hits beyond line 70; a targeted search for "CONVERSAS" found exactly this one line). **The prototype extract is silent on exact visual tokens for the session-list rows** (per-row padding, divider style, active/selected-session highlight state, timestamp format) — per AGENTS.md policy this will need a per-spec decision, likely by reusing `_DrawerNavItem`'s existing padding/typography tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, etc., from `app_drawer.dart:195-213`) rather than inventing new tokens.
  - Line 223 mentions the initials Avatar component sizing (40px in menu) — already used in the drawer header, not session-row-specific.
  
  ## 7. Existing test conventions for chat
  
  Existing chat test files (all present):
  - `test/features/chat/chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`
  - `test/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source_test.dart`
  - `test/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart`
  - `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`
  - `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart`
  - `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart`
  
  `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart` DI-override/fake-repository pattern — **confirmed still present, but line numbers have shifted from the "257-268" cited in spec-6-1** (the file has grown since). Current locations:
  - `_FakeChatRepository` class: **lines 128-156** (doc comment 120-127 explains rationale: `listSessions()` always returns one session so `ChatCubit.init()` settles on `ChatReady` without hitting `createSession()`/`sendMessage()`; this suite never exercises chat behavior itself, only that the router's `GoRoute.builder` resolves).
  - `listSessions()` stub: 130-140 (one fake session, `id: 'fake-session'`).
  - `createSession()` stub: 143-144 — deliberately `throw UnimplementedError('not expected to be called')`.
  - `listMessages()` stub: 147-149 — always `right(const [])`.
  - `sendMessage()` stub: 152-155 — `const Stream.empty()`.
  - Registration of `ChatCubit` with this fake into `sl`: **line 331** (`sl.registerLazySingleton<ChatCubit>(() => ChatCubit(_FakeChatRepository()), ...)`), inside `setUp`/router-builder wiring starting around line 278.
  - 6.2 should mirror this same fake-repository-via-constructor-injection pattern (confirmed still the house convention) when adding tests for session-switch/new-session cubit methods and drawer-list rendering — most likely by extending `_FakeChatRepository` or writing a comparable fake in `chat_cubit_test.dart`/a new drawer test file, not by mocking `ChatRepository` with mocktail (the codebase favors plain fakes for this interface per the comment on line 158-161 regarding a different fake, and per `ChatScreen`'s own doc at `chat_screen.dart:18-21` about accepting `cubit` directly for test substitution).
  
  ## 8. Scroll-position persistence precedent
  
  - **No existing pattern for persisting/restoring a scroll offset across a widget being unmounted and remounted (or across switching logical "lists") exists anywhere in `lib/`.** Grep for `ScrollController|scrollOffset|jumpTo|keepScrollOffset|PageStorageKey` across `lib/` returns only:
    - `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:66` — `final ScrollController _scrollController = ScrollController();`, and `:538` — a `scrollController` field threaded into a child widget for pagination (`onRetryLoadMore`-style infinite-scroll trigger), **not** position save/restore. Confirmed by reading context at lines 60-70 and 530-545 — this controller exists purely to detect "near end of list, fetch next page," with no offset persistence.
    - `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:33` — `_scrollController = ScrollController()`, created fresh every mount (33), disposed every unmount (46), with `_scrollToBottomSoon()` (59-79) only handling "stick to bottom while streaming" — not restore-last-position.
  - **Conclusion: Story 6.2's "restore last conversation's scroll position when opened" AC has zero precedent to mirror in this codebase.** This will need a new mechanism from scratch — options to weigh in the spec: (a) `ChatCubit`/`ChatState` keeps a `Map<String sessionId, double offset>` in memory, written on scroll/dispose and applied via `jumpTo` after the `ListView` for that session rebuilds; (b) a `PageStorageKey` keyed by `sessionId` on the `ListView.builder` (`chat_screen.dart:110-118`) if Flutter's own `PageStorage` scroll-position caching is judged sufficient (works automatically across teardown/rebuild if the same `BuildContext`/`PageStorageBucket` is retained, but the router's route-rebuild behavior should be checked since `ChatCubit` is a lazy singleton surviving screen disposal — the `ChatScreen`'s own `State` and its `ScrollController` do *not* survive unmount, so `PageStorageKey` is the only candidate that doesn't require cubit-side state unless (a) is chosen).
  
  ## Cross-cutting note
  
  Several of the exact names/sections requested don't exist verbatim in the files named in the prompt — flagged explicitly above rather than silently substituted: "FR-24" is an `epics.md`-only label, not a `requirements.md` section; the "offline composer lock" the Story 6.2 AC references is a Story 6.3 (not-yet-built) UI mechanism; and `app_router_test.dart`'s fake-chat-repository pattern has moved to lines 128-156 (not 257-268).
