 - source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
   summary: `Hive.openBox<Map>(...)` calls are unguarded (no try/catch) across the codebase — a corrupted/locked box would crash app startup — surfaced here for `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart`'s two new boxes, but the exact same unguarded pattern already exists in `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart:28` and presumably every other `hive_ce` box opened at DI time.
   evidence: `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart:28` (`final entriesBox = await Hive.openBox<Map>(entriesBoxName);`, no surrounding try/catch) confirms this predates story 6.1 and is a cross-cutting Hive-resilience gap, not something chat introduced — worth a dedicated hardening pass across all features rather than a one-off fix inside chat's own injection file.
+
+## Deferred from: code review of story-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response, round 2 (2026-11-05)
+
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: `_ChatBootstrapErrorView` renders every bootstrap-failure cause (offline, timeout, server error) identically via `colorError`, even though the spec's own Code Map lists `colorInfoOffline` as a relevant token for this story and it's never referenced anywhere in the diff.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:173-204`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). No acceptance criterion requires differentiated styling per failure cause — the I/O matrix only asks for "a generic error state, not infinite spinner," which is satisfied. Revisit as a deliberate visual pass if distinguishing offline from server-error bootstrap failures proves useful in practice.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: `ChatScreen`'s `BlocConsumer` listener calls `_scrollToBottomSoon()` on every `ChatReady` emission, which fires once per streamed token during a response — a long AI reply registers a fresh `addPostFrameCallback` on nearly every frame.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:64`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Harmless today (cheap, idempotent `jumpTo`, no observed jank), but unthrottled; 6.2+ will add more state onto this same `ChatReady`. Revisit with debouncing if streaming performance proves disruptive in practice.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: The composer's client-side 8000-char cap (`TextField(maxLength: 8000, ...)`) assumes the backend counts `content` length the same way Flutter's `maxLength` does.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:253`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Nothing in this diff confirms the backend's own counting unit (bytes vs. code points vs. grapheme clusters), and this can't be verified from the client repo alone — same "can't verify without the other side's source" class as the `whisper_ggml`/`downloadModel` entry above. Revisit if surrogate-pair-heavy (emoji-heavy) messages are ever rejected despite passing the client-side check.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: No test drives an `authExpired` bootstrap failure through `ChatCubit`/`ChatScreen`.
+  evidence: `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`. Review finding (code-review, verification-gap layer). The underlying re-auth-overlay trigger is already covered generically by Story 1.5's `ApiClient._mapDioException` test group, which `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` all go through unchanged — so this is a thin-spot regression test for chat's own bootstrap path, not a live gap in the trigger mechanism itself.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: The streaming AI bubble (`ChatBubble`) renders growing text via plain `Text.rich` with no `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` — a screen-reader user gets no incremental announcement while tokens stream in.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Same unaddressed accessibility pattern already deferred for `Avatar`/nav icons/`EntryRecordCard` (Stories 1.2/1.6/4.1's own deferred-work entries) — no accessibility requirement is scoped for this story either; worth the same deliberate future pass.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: The two new `chat_sessions`/`chat_messages` Hive boxes accumulate every session/message ever fetched, with no eviction/TTL.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Same unbounded-growth pattern already deferred for the `entries` Hive box (spec-4-1's own deferred-work entry) — not called out anywhere in the spec or epic-context as a future concern, so flagging here so it isn't forgotten once Story 6.2 (multi-session history) starts growing this data faster.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-1-send-message-receive-rag-grounded-streaming-response.md`
+  summary: `ChatCubit.sendMessage()`'s internal `await completer.future` is never awaited by its only caller (`ChatScreen._send()`), making the method effectively fire-and-forget from the UI.
+  evidence: `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:55`. Review finding (code-review, blind-hunter layer). Harmless today — nothing throws after that await point — but a future story (6.5's insight-trigger counting is the named candidate) adding logic after it inside `sendMessage()` would have its errors/results silently dropped unless the call site starts awaiting or the method's contract changes.

 ## Design Notes
 
 - SSE per-event field names aren't specified beyond the ordering `message_created→context→token*→done|error` (openapi.yaml:1257) — this spec assumes `token` carries a `delta` text field and `message_created` carries the persisted user-message id; anything that fails to parse as expected becomes `Failure.malformedResponse`, never a crash.

+- Session bootstrap (list-or-create one session) is a minimal stand-in for Story 6.2's real session management: *which* session is the active one is kept in memory only (`ChatReady.sessionId`), never written to Hive as a dedicated "active session" record, so 6.2 can own that persistence shape without migrating this story's data. By contrast, the exact same fix for the *offline-cache* fallback is tested directly: `test/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart:129-149` ("one corrupted cache entry is skipped"). I also checked the new e2e file `test/features/chat/chat_flow_e2e_test.dart` — its `_sessionJson` helper only ever produces valid shapes, so it doesn't exercise this branch either.

  - **Suggested test shape:** a `chat_remote_data_source_test.dart` case feeding `listSessions()`/`listMessages()` a `data` array with one well-formed item and one malformed item, asserting `Right` with only the good item retained — same shape as the existing cache-fallback test.
  
  ### `sendMessage()`'s \r\n-across-chunk-boundary buffer fix is unverified
  
  - **Changed surface:** `buffer = (buffer + chunk).replaceAll('\r\n', '\n')` — normalization now happens after concatenation, fixing the case where a `\r\n` line ending is split exactly across two network chunks (one ends `\r`, the next starts `\n`) — `lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:133`. Previously it normalized each chunk before appending.
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** the SSE event parser's `\n\n`-boundary split immediately below (`buffer.indexOf('\n\n')`), which a surviving literal `\r\n` would cause to miss or misparse.
  - **Existing test evidence:** I read the `sendMessage — SSE parsing` group in `test/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source_test.dart:134-343` and the new e2e file. The "chunks split mid-event" test (lines 184-216) splits mid-event-name and mid-data-field, but never splits a `\r\n` pair across chunks — in fact I grepped the whole `test/features/chat/` tree for `\r` and found zero matches anywhere.
  - **Missing verification:** a test that queues two chunks where the first ends in `\r` and the second starts with `\n` (completing a `\r\n` event terminator), asserting the event still parses correctly.
  - **Demonstration:** reverting to per-chunk normalization (`buffer += chunk.replaceAll(...)`) would pass every existing test, since none of them ever produces a `\r` at a chunk boundary.
  - **Consequence:** a regression reintroducing per-chunk normalization would ship with no test catching the exact bug this fix was written for.
  - **Suggested test shape:** `stubPostStream` with `['event: done\r', '\ndata: {}\r\n\r\n']` (or similar), asserting the event is still recognized.

  - **Changed surface:** three sites switched from `String.compareTo` to `DateTime.parse(...).compareTo(...)` on `updatedAt` for "most recent session" ordering: `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:98` (bootstrap "reuse most recent"), `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:143` (`_cachedSessions` offline sort), and the new `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:328` (`_ConversasSection`'s defensive re-sort).
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** all three — session-bootstrap reuse, offline session list ordering, and the drawer's CONVERSAS ordering.
  - **Existing test evidence:** I checked every test touching these sorts: `chat_cubit_test.dart:74-96` (bootstrap reuse), `chat_repository_impl_test.dart:77-95` (offline sort), and `app_drawer_test.dart` (CONVERSAS ordering via `_sessionA`/`_sessionB`). Every one of them uses uniform fixed-width ISO-8601 timestamps like `'2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'` / `'2026-01-03T00:00:00Z'` — same format, same length — where lexicographic and chronological ordering always agree.
  - **Missing verification:** a case with timestamps that differ in format/precision (e.g. one with a fractional-second suffix, or a non-`Z` offset) where string-order and date-order diverge, which is exactly the scenario the fix exists to handle.
  - **Demonstration:** reverting any of the three sites back to raw `String.compareTo` on `updatedAt` would not make any of the tests I checked fail, because every fixture's timestamps happen to sort identically either way.
  - **Consequence:** a regression back to naive string comparison on `updatedAt` — which would silently reorder "most recent" session selection whenever timestamp formatting isn't perfectly uniform — ships with no test able to catch it.
  - **Suggested test shape:** one fixture pair per site with mismatched timestamp formatting (e.g. `'2026-01-01T09:59:59.999Z'` vs `'2026-01-01T10:00:00+01:00'`) where only a true `DateTime` comparison picks the chronologically-later one.

  - **Changed surface:** `_ChatScreenState`'s `BlocConsumer` listener now tracks `_lastSessionId` to detect a session switch (`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:153`), and on a genuine switch either calls `_jumpToOffset(state.restoreScrollOffset)` (line 161) or falls back to `_scrollToBottomSoon()`, then calls `_focusComposerSoon()` (line 166) when the new session is empty. A new `_recordScrollOffset` listener (line 67) feeds `ChatCubit.recordScrollOffset` on every scroll update.
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** this is the only consumer of `ChatReady.sessionId`-change detection, `ChatReady.restoreScrollOffset`, and `ChatCubit.recordScrollOffset` at the UI layer — the entire feature only does something observable here.
  - **Existing test evidence:** I read `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` in full (283 lines) — it predates spec-6-2, builds `ChatScreen` directly, and never exercises `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, never checks `FocusNode.hasFocus`, and never checks scroll position. I also read `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` — its router builds a bare `Scaffold(drawer: AppDrawer())`, not the real `ChatScreen`, so even though it exercises `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` through real taps, nothing observes what `ChatScreen` does in reaction. I grepped the whole `test/` tree for `_jumpToOffset`, `_focusComposerSoon`, `composerFocusNode`, `requestFocus`, and `recordScrollOffset` — the only hits are the cubit-level test (`chat_cubit_test.dart:295,300,305`, which calls `cubit.recordScrollOffset` directly and checks the resulting state field, never the screen's listener wiring) and unrelated matches in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`.
  - **Missing verification:** a widget test that drives a real `switchSession`/`startNewSession` through `ChatScreen` (not just through the bare-Scaffold `AppDrawer` harness) and asserts the composer gains focus for a new empty session, or that the scroll position jumps to a previously recorded offset for a resumed session.
  - **Demonstration:** if `isNewSession` were inverted, or `_focusComposerSoon`/`_jumpToOffset` were never wired to fire, every test I read would still pass — none of them pumps `ChatScreen` through a session switch and inspects focus or scroll state afterward.
  - **Consequence:** a regression that silently breaks "new chat opens with composer focused" or "switching back to a session restores its scroll position" — both explicit acceptance criteria for this story — would ship with the full suite green.
  - **Suggested test shape:** extend `chat_screen_test.dart` with a case using a `_FakeChatRepository` that supports `createSession`/`listMessages` for a second session, driving `ChatScreen` end to end (tap the real "+Novo Chat" affordance or call `widget.cubit.startNewSession()` directly against the pumped screen) and asserting `_composerFocusNode`-equivalent focus state and `_scrollController.position.pixels` after a switch.
  
  ### `ChatCubit.close()`'s in-flight-completer fix is only exercised in a scenario where it's a no-op
  
  - **Changed surface:** `close()` now explicitly completes `_sendCompleter` if it's non-null and not yet completed, because `_sendSubscription?.cancel()` never fires `onDone`/`onError` — `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:385-392`.
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `ChatCubit.sendMessage()`'s own returned `Future` (the `Completer` created at line ~265), for any future caller that awaits it.
  - **Existing test evidence:** I read every `close()`-related test in `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`. The closest, at lines 498-532, calls `staleRepository.lastSendController!.close()` *before* `await staleCubit.close()` — closing the stream controller first fires the normal `onDone` callback, which already completes and nulls out `_sendCompleter` through the pre-existing path, so by the time `close()` runs there is nothing left for its new explicit-complete branch to do. No test leaves the stream open (controller never closed) and then calls `cubit.close()` while checking that the original `sendMessage()` future still resolves.
  - **Missing verification:** a test that calls `sendMessage()`, does *not* close/emit on the fake stream, calls `await cubit.close()`, and asserts the `Future` returned by `sendMessage()` completes (e.g. within a timeout) rather than hanging.
  - **Demonstration:** reverting `close()` to just `_sendSubscription?.cancel(); return super.close();` (dropping the explicit completer completion) would not make the test at lines 498-532 fail, since that test's completer is already resolved via `onDone` before `close()` is even reached.
  - **Consequence:** a regression that drops this explicit-completion fix would leave `sendMessage()`'s Future permanently unresolved whenever the cubit closes mid-send with the stream still open — exactly the bug this patch fixed — and ship with the suite green. (Noted in the diff's own `deferred-work.md` that no current caller awaits this Future, so the leak is currently inert — but the fix itself is still unverified.)
  - **Suggested test shape:** call `sendMessage()` without closing/completing the fake repository's stream controller, then `await cubit.close().timeout(...)` together with awaiting the `sendMessage()` future, asserting it completes rather than timing out.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

input.summary: Apply code-review patch findings to spec 6-2
input.message:
Code review of your spec-6-2 implementation surfaced 4 "patch" findings (trivially-fixable, confirmed real) that need fixing now. Apply all four:

1. **Cross-session stream leakage (high severity).** `ChatCubit.switchSession()` and `startNewSession()` don't cancel the in-flight `_sendSubscription` or check `_isSending` before switching the active session. If a user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while an AI response is still streaming, the orphaned subscription's `onData`/`onDone` callbacks keep firing and apply token/done events to whatever session is now active — cross-session message corruption. Fix: at the top of both `switchSession()` and `startNewSession()`, if `_isSending` is true, do the same cleanup `close()` already does — cancel `_sendSubscription`, complete+null `_sendCompleter` if pending, reset `_isSending = false` — before proceeding with the switch/create. Add a regression test in `chat_cubit_test.dart` that starts a send (don't let the fake stream complete), then calls `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, and asserts the old stream's late-arriving events never mutate the new active session's state.

2. **Crash risk in the new `_ConversasSection` sort.** `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`'s new `_ConversasSection` sorts sessions via `DateTime.parse(b.updatedAt).compareTo(DateTime.parse(a.updatedAt))` — an uncaught `FormatException` on a malformed `updatedAt` crashes the whole drawer build. Fix: use the same crash-safe pattern already sitting right next to it in the same file (`_formatSessionTimestamp`'s `DateTime.tryParse(...)` fallback) — e.g. `(DateTime.tryParse(b.updatedAt) ?? DateTime(0)).compareTo(DateTime.tryParse(a.updatedAt) ?? DateTime(0))`. Add a widget test with a session carrying a malformed `updatedAt` string, asserting the drawer still renders instead of throwing.

3. **Zero screen-level test coverage for 2 of this story's 4 acceptance criteria.** `ChatScreen`'s own `_lastSessionId`/`_jumpToOffset`/`_focusComposerSoon` wiring — the actual implementation of "new session opens with composer focused" and "returning session restores scroll position" — is never exercised by any test that pumps the real `ChatScreen` through a session switch. Existing tests only check `ChatCubit`'s state field directly (`chat_cubit_test.dart`) or drive `AppDrawer` against a bare `Scaffold` with no real `ChatScreen` underneath (`app_drawer_test.dart`). Fix: add a case (or two) to `test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart` that drives a real `switchSession`/`startNewSession` through a pumped `ChatScreen` (via a fake repository with 2+ sessions) and asserts (a) the composer's `FocusNode` gains focus when a new empty session becomes active, and (b) `_scrollController`'s position reflects a previously recorded offset when switching back to a session that had one.

4. **Inaccurate doc comment.** `ChatScreen`'s `_focusComposerSoon()` doc comment claims it's "only ever called right after a *new* session ... becomes active with no messages yet, never on an ordinary switch to a past (non-empty) session" — but the actual guard is just `state.messages.isEmpty`, so switching to any past session that happens to be empty also triggers it. The behavior is fine (focusing composer on an empty past session isn't wrong), only the comment overclaims. Fix: reword the comment to describe the actual guard (`messages.isEmpty`) rather than claiming it's exclusive to brand-new sessions.

After applying all four: re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (all pass, including your new regression tests), then report back what changed and the verification output.

input.old_string: ## Spec Change Log
input.new_string:
### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatCubit.switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` didn't cancel an in-flight `_sendSubscription` or check `_isSending` before switching the active session — a response still streaming into the old session kept mutating whatever session became active next (cross-session message leakage). Fixed via a new `_cancelInFlightSend()`, mirroring `close()`'s own cleanup. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_ConversasSection`'s new sort used `DateTime.parse` (not `tryParse`) on `updatedAt` — a malformed timestamp crashed the whole drawer build. Fixed to the same crash-safe `tryParse` pattern already used by `_formatSessionTimestamp` next to it. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart] (Same pattern also found and fixed in the pre-existing, untouched `ChatCubit._bootstrap` sort, which blocked exercising this very fix — disclosed by the implementer, not one of the original four findings.)
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test drove `ChatScreen` itself (only `ChatCubit`'s state field or a bare-`Scaffold` drawer harness) through a session switch, leaving 2 of this story's 4 acceptance criteria (composer-focus-on-new-session, scroll-restore-on-switch) unverified at the layer that implements them. Added screen-level tests to `chat_screen_test.dart`. [test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_focusComposerSoon`'s doc comment overclaimed it only fires for a brand-new session, when the actual guard (`messages.isEmpty`) also fires when switching back to an empty past session. Comment corrected. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart]

**Defer:** 11 findings (UX nits, pre-existing-code verification gaps surfaced incidentally, duplication) appended to `deferred-work.md` under "review of story-6-2-multi-session-chat-history-new-conversation".

**Reject (noise, dropped):** `restoreScrollOffset`'s inability to be reset to `null` via `copyWith` — already documented as deliberate in this spec's own Design Notes; not a bug.

1	---
2	title: 'Story 6.2 — Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-05'
5	status: 'in-review'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	baseline_commit: '53de1f87bba2564a87e998b7bb1a515068dd299a'

9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Home/Chat (story 6.1) hard-codes a single auto-bootstrapped session with no way to see past sessions or start a fresh one; `AppDrawer` has no session list at all, just a dead "Novo Chat" button.
16	
17	**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` methods that reuse the existing `listSessions()`/`createSession()` repository calls (already backend-correct — no data-layer change needed), carry the session list and a per-session scroll offset on `ChatReady`, and wire `AppDrawer`'s missing "CONVERSAS" section to read/call that same cubit instance via the `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>` already wrapping the drawer's `Scaffold`.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Drawer reads `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder` — the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` (`chat_screen.dart:83-87`); never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()` inside `AppDrawer`.
23	- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`, `await`ed by their `AppDrawer` tap handlers (closes a gap spec-6-1's review flagged: a cubit action's result must be observed by its caller).
24	- Offline "Novo Chat" leaves the current session untouched; caller shows a transient `SnackBar`, not a dedicated offline banner (Story 6.3's job).
25	- Scroll-offset restore is in-memory only, keyed by `sessionId`, on `ChatCubit` (never Hive) — survives session switches within one app run, resets on restart.
26	- Reuse `_DrawerNavItem`'s tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, `textMonoCaption`) — no new design tokens.
27	- An empty `title` renders fallback label "Nova conversa" (contract leaves an untitled session's `title` undocumented).
28	
29	**Ask First:** none identified.
30	
31	**Never:** session rename/delete (no endpoint); paginating past the backend's default first page; Story 6.3's offline composer lock/banner; persisting scroll offset or active-session choice across app restarts.
32	
33	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
34	
35	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
36	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
37	| Switch session | Drawer open, tap a past session row | `ChatReady` updates to that session's history; scroll jumps to its last recorded offset (or bottom if none) | N/A |
38	| New session online | Tap "Novo Chat" while online | `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds; new empty session becomes active, composer focused, drawer closes | N/A |
39	| New session offline | Tap "Novo Chat" while offline | `createSession()` resolves `Left(Failure.networkOffline)`; current session stays active, drawer closes, `SnackBar` shown | `Failure.networkOffline` surfaced, no crash |
40	| Switch to already-active session | Tap the currently open session's own row | No-op reload; drawer just closes | N/A |
41	
42	</frozen-after-approval>
43	
44	## Code Map
45	
46	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:40-69` -- `ChatReady`: add `sessions: List<ChatSession>`, `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; extend `copyWith`.
47	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:64-114` (`_bootstrap`) -- capture resolved sessions into the emitted `ChatReady`; add `Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets`, `recordScrollOffset`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession` (mirror `_bootstrap`'s match-based error handling, lines 92-113).
48	- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:21,31` -- `listSessions()`/`createSession()`, reused as-is.
49	- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:17-131` -- wrap body in `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`; insert a "CONVERSAS" section (mirrors bordered `Container`, lines 78-108) between `_DrawerPrimaryAction` (65-71) and it, shown only when `state is ChatReady`; wire `_DrawerPrimaryAction.onTap` (70) to `startNewSession()`.
50	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:33,59-79` -- on `ChatReady.restoreScrollOffset != null`, `jumpTo` it once instead of `_scrollToBottomSoon()`; add a listener calling `cubit.recordScrollOffset`.
51	- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1071-1155` -- confirms no rename/delete/pagination-required endpoint.
52	- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156` -- `_FakeChatRepository`, the DI-override pattern to extend.
53	
54	## Tasks & Acceptance
55	
56	**Execution:**
57	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- add `sessions`/`restoreScrollOffset` to `ChatReady` -- no second state container (AD-12).
58	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- add `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `recordScrollOffset`; populate `sessions` in `_bootstrap` -- one cubit stays the source of truth.
59	- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- render CONVERSAS from `ChatReady.sessions`, wire tap → `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, `await` + `SnackBar` on `Left` -- closes the gap at doc-comment lines 8-16.
60	- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- scroll-offset capture + restore-on-switch -- fulfils the scroll-position AC.
61	- [x] `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` -- unit-test `switchSession`/`startNewSession`/offline-create/no-op-on-same-session per the I/O matrix.
62	- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` (pre-existing from Story 1.6, rewritten in place rather than duplicated — its old assertions asserted the now-obsolete "no CONVERSAS section" behavior) -- widget tests: CONVERSAS rendering, tap-to-switch, offline `SnackBar`, mirroring `_FakeChatRepository` (`app_router_test.dart:128-156`).
63	
64	**Acceptance Criteria:**
65	- Given existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they're listed under "CONVERSAS" and tapping one switches the active conversation.
66	- Given I tap "Novo Chat", when the new session is created, then it opens empty, composer focused, placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...".
67	- Given I'm offline, when I tap "Novo Chat", then no session is created, the current conversation is untouched, and I see an error message.
68	- Given I switch back to a session I was previously scrolled up in, when it loads, then it restores that scroll position instead of jumping to the bottom.
69	
70	## Design Notes
71	
72	- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` don't re-emit `ChatBootstrapLoading` (a 4th visible state isn't worth it — "exactly three" governs bubbles, not session-switch chrome). `_scrollOffsets` lives on the long-lived cubit (`chat_injection.dart:50-53`), not `ChatReady`.
73	
74	## Verification
75	
76	**Commands:**
77	- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
78	- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass, including new cubit/drawer tests

## Intent

**Problem:** Home/Chat (story 6.1) hard-codes a single auto-bootstrapped session with no way to see past sessions or start a fresh one; `AppDrawer` has no session list at all, just a dead "Novo Chat" button.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` methods that reuse the existing `listSessions()`/`createSession()` repository calls (already backend-correct — no data-layer change needed), carry the session list and a per-session scroll offset on `ChatReady`, and wire `AppDrawer`'s missing "CONVERSAS" section to read/call that same cubit instance via the `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>` already wrapping the drawer's `Scaffold`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**

- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`, `await`ed by their `AppDrawer` tap handlers (closes a gap spec-6-1's review flagged: a cubit action's result must be observed by its caller).
- Offline "Novo Chat" leaves the current session untouched; caller shows a transient `SnackBar`, not a dedicated offline banner (Story 6.3's job).
- Scroll-offset restore is in-memory only, keyed by `sessionId`, on `ChatCubit` (never Hive) — survives session switches within one app run, resets on restart.
- Reuse `_DrawerNavItem`'s tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, `textMonoCaption`) — no new design tokens.
- An empty `title` renders fallback label "Nova conversa" (contract leaves an untitled session's `title` undocumented).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:** session rename/delete (no endpoint); paginating past the backend's default first page; Story 6.3's offline composer lock/banner; persisting scroll offset or active-session choice across app restarts.

| Switch to already-active session | Tap the currently open session's own row | No-op reload; drawer just closes | N/A |

---
title: 'Story 6.2 — Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'in-review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '53de1f87bba2564a87e998b7bb1a515068dd299a'
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Home/Chat (story 6.1) hard-codes a single auto-bootstrapped session with no way to see past sessions or start a fresh one; `AppDrawer` has no session list at all, just a dead "Novo Chat" button.

**Approach:** Add `ChatCubit.switchSession`/`startNewSession` methods that reuse the existing `listSessions()`/`createSession()` repository calls (already backend-correct — no data-layer change needed), carry the session list and a per-session scroll offset on `ChatReady`, and wire `AppDrawer`'s missing "CONVERSAS" section to read/call that same cubit instance via the `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>` already wrapping the drawer's `Scaffold`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Drawer reads `context.read<ChatCubit>()`/`BlocBuilder` — the instance `ChatScreen` already provides via `BlocProvider<ChatCubit>.value` (`chat_screen.dart:83-87`); never a second `sl<ChatCubit>()` inside `AppDrawer`.
- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` return `Future<Either<Failure, void>>`, `await`ed by their `AppDrawer` tap handlers (closes a gap spec-6-1's review flagged: a cubit action's result must be observed by its caller).
- Offline "Novo Chat" leaves the current session untouched; caller shows a transient `SnackBar`, not a dedicated offline banner (Story 6.3's job).
- Scroll-offset restore is in-memory only, keyed by `sessionId`, on `ChatCubit` (never Hive) — survives session switches within one app run, resets on restart.
- Reuse `_DrawerNavItem`'s tokens (`drawerNavItemPadding`, `textBodyMd`, `textMonoCaption`) — no new design tokens.
- An empty `title` renders fallback label "Nova conversa" (contract leaves an untitled session's `title` undocumented).

**Ask First:** none identified.

**Never:** session rename/delete (no endpoint); paginating past the backend's default first page; Story 6.3's offline composer lock/banner; persisting scroll offset or active-session choice across app restarts.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Switch session | Drawer open, tap a past session row | `ChatReady` updates to that session's history; scroll jumps to its last recorded offset (or bottom if none) | N/A |
| New session online | Tap "Novo Chat" while online | `POST /chat/sessions` succeeds; new empty session becomes active, composer focused, drawer closes | N/A |
| New session offline | Tap "Novo Chat" while offline | `createSession()` resolves `Left(Failure.networkOffline)`; current session stays active, drawer closes, `SnackBar` shown | `Failure.networkOffline` surfaced, no crash |
| Switch to already-active session | Tap the currently open session's own row | No-op reload; drawer just closes | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:40-69` -- `ChatReady`: add `sessions: List<ChatSession>`, `restoreScrollOffset: double?`; extend `copyWith`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:64-114` (`_bootstrap`) -- capture resolved sessions into the emitted `ChatReady`; add `Map<String, double> _scrollOffsets`, `recordScrollOffset`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession` (mirror `_bootstrap`'s match-based error handling, lines 92-113).
- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart:21,31` -- `listSessions()`/`createSession()`, reused as-is.
- `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart:17-131` -- wrap body in `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>`; insert a "CONVERSAS" section (mirrors bordered `Container`, lines 78-108) between `_DrawerPrimaryAction` (65-71) and it, shown only when `state is ChatReady`; wire `_DrawerPrimaryAction.onTap` (70) to `startNewSession()`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart:33,59-79` -- on `ChatReady.restoreScrollOffset != null`, `jumpTo` it once instead of `_scrollToBottomSoon()`; add a listener calling `cubit.recordScrollOffset`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:1071-1155` -- confirms no rename/delete/pagination-required endpoint.
- `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart:128-156` -- `_FakeChatRepository`, the DI-override pattern to extend.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` -- add `sessions`/`restoreScrollOffset` to `ChatReady` -- no second state container (AD-12).
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` -- add `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `recordScrollOffset`; populate `sessions` in `_bootstrap` -- one cubit stays the source of truth.
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` -- render CONVERSAS from `ChatReady.sessions`, wire tap → `switchSession`/`startNewSession`, `await` + `SnackBar` on `Left` -- closes the gap at doc-comment lines 8-16.
- [x] `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- scroll-offset capture + restore-on-switch -- fulfils the scroll-position AC.
- [x] `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` -- unit-test `switchSession`/`startNewSession`/offline-create/no-op-on-same-session per the I/O matrix.
- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart` (pre-existing from Story 1.6, rewritten in place rather than duplicated — its old assertions asserted the now-obsolete "no CONVERSAS section" behavior) -- widget tests: CONVERSAS rendering, tap-to-switch, offline `SnackBar`, mirroring `_FakeChatRepository` (`app_router_test.dart:128-156`).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given existing Chat Sessions, when I open the side menu, then they're listed under "CONVERSAS" and tapping one switches the active conversation.
- Given I tap "Novo Chat", when the new session is created, then it opens empty, composer focused, placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...".
- Given I'm offline, when I tap "Novo Chat", then no session is created, the current conversation is untouched, and I see an error message.
- Given I switch back to a session I was previously scrolled up in, when it loads, then it restores that scroll position instead of jumping to the bottom.

### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [x] [Review][Patch] `ChatCubit.switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` didn't cancel an in-flight `_sendSubscription` or check `_isSending` before switching the active session — a response still streaming into the old session kept mutating whatever session became active next (cross-session message leakage). Fixed via a new `_cancelInFlightSend()`, mirroring `close()`'s own cleanup. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_ConversasSection`'s new sort used `DateTime.parse` (not `tryParse`) on `updatedAt` — a malformed timestamp crashed the whole drawer build. Fixed to the same crash-safe `tryParse` pattern already used by `_formatSessionTimestamp` next to it. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart] (The same pattern, found and fixed in the pre-existing, otherwise-untouched `ChatCubit._bootstrap` sort, blocked exercising this very fix — disclosed by the implementer, not one of the original four findings.)
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test drove `ChatScreen` itself (only `ChatCubit`'s state field or a bare-`Scaffold` drawer harness) through a session switch, leaving 2 of this story's 4 acceptance criteria (composer-focus-on-new-session, scroll-restore-on-switch) unverified at the layer that implements them. Added screen-level tests to `chat_screen_test.dart`. [test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `_focusComposerSoon`'s doc comment overclaimed it only fires for a brand-new session, when the actual guard (`messages.isEmpty`) also fires when switching back to an empty past session. Comment corrected. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart]

**Defer:** 11 findings (UX nits, pre-existing-code verification gaps surfaced incidentally by this review, cross-site duplication) appended to `deferred-work.md` under "review of story-6-2-multi-session-chat-history-new-conversation".

**Reject (noise, dropped):** `restoreScrollOffset`'s inability to be reset to `null` via `copyWith` — already documented as deliberate in this spec's own Design Notes; not a bug.

## Spec Change Log

## Design Notes

- `switchSession`/`startNewSession` don't re-emit `ChatBootstrapLoading` (a 4th visible state isn't worth it — "exactly three" governs bubbles, not session-switch chrome). `_scrollOffsets` lives on the long-lived cubit (`chat_injection.dart:50-53`), not `ChatReady`.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
